blocks.content: A judge of a High Court can be removed from his office by an order of the President.

rows: Speaker may admit or refuse the motion
Chairman may admit or refuse the motion

items: High Court judges are appointed by the President and can ONLY be removed by the President, not the Governor.
The process and grounds for removal of a High Court judge are exactly the same as those for a Supreme Court judge.
The Speaker or Chairman has the discretion to admit or refuse to admit the removal motion even if signed by the requisite number of members.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: A judge of a High Court can be removed from office only by an order of the President passed after an address by Parliament.
The grounds for removal are limited to two: proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
The motion must be supported by a special majority in each House of Parliament (majority of total membership and 2/3rd of members present and voting).
The procedure for investigation and proof of misbehaviour or incapacity is governed by the Judges Enquiry Act, 1968.
No judge of a High Court has been impeached/removed so far in the constitutional history of India.
